newsitem.title: GERMANY: 27th-generation German vineyard owner found dead.
newsitem.headline: 27th-generation German vineyard owner found dead.

text.p: The 27th-generation owner of one of Germany's oldest and best-known vineyards, Schloss Vollrads, was found dead with a revolver by his side on Tuesday, police said.
A suicide note believed to have been written by 58-year-old Erwein Graf Matuschka-Greiffenclau, whose body was found near his castle, cited financial problems.
"I have made commercial mistakes and I must pay for them," said the note discovered inside the castle, according to police in the central German state of Hesse.
Separately, credit institute Nassauer Sparkasse said it had issued a petition on Monday to begin bankruptcy proceedings against the vineyard.
Earlier this year it emerged that Schloss Vollrads had fallen into financial difficulties due to the heavy cost of maintaining the historic castle that gave the vineyard its name.
